sports.head: DANGER ROOM FINAL ENDS IN SPIKES
sports.body: The annual danger-room wrestling final ended 4-4 after both finalists were struck by the same upright spear trap. Referees ruled it a draw, the trap was declared man of the match, and the trophy was sent to the hospital for safekeeping.

sports.head: HAULING RELAY SETS NEW SLOWEST TIME
sports.body: The stone-hauling relay finished in a record nine days after the second runner stopped mid-lap to pick up a sock, store it, return, and resume. Officials confirmed this is legal. The baton, a granite boulder, has been placed in a stockpile.

sports.head: MUG-THROWING OPEN DRAWS HOSTILE CROWD
sports.body: Competitors at this season's mug-throwing open scored points for distance, spin and emotional sincerity. The winner, mid-tantrum, cleared the dining hall in a single toss. Organisers remind fans that catching a mug with your face does not count as participation.

sports.head: CAVE-SWIMMING GOLD GOES TO NOBODY
sports.body: No swimmer completed the underground river course this year. The leader reached the halfway marker before remembering he could not swim, a skill he had listed as 'Dabbling'. He was retrieved by bucket brigade, final score Swimmers 0, River 6.

sports.head: CARP-DODGING SEMIS: CARP UNDEFEATED
sports.body: The carp-dodging semifinals were abandoned after the carp advanced to the final themselves. League officials have asked the carp to sign a code of conduct. The carp responded by biting the clipboard, the official, and the official's cousin.

sports.head: MINECART DERBY HITS 40 URISTS PER HOUR
sports.body: The minecart derby was won by a rider who did not technically intend to enter. Witnesses say the track ended in a wall, which he reached first. He is in good spirits and fair condition, and has asked that the wall be awarded silver.

sports.head: COMPETITIVE BROODING: A TENSE STARE-OFF
sports.body: Finalists in the competitive brooding championship stared at the same wall for sixteen hours. Judges scored the frowns on depth, menace and beard involvement. The eventual winner was a dwarf who had not realised the competition had started, or ended.

sports.head: LEAGUE TABLE: MILITIA SLIPS TO THIRD
sports.body: The latest league table shows the militia in third place behind the Brewers and the Cats, who have not played a match but are listed anyway because nobody can remove them. The Training Dummies remain bottom without conceding a complaint.

sports.head: SPARRING INJURY REPORT: EVERYONE
sports.body: This week's injury report lists every member of the militia as doubtful, including the captain, who sprained something while reading the injury report. Squad training continues. Fans are reminded that a broken leg is just the leg doing its best.

sports.head: WELL-DIVING CHAMPIONSHIP CANCELLED
sports.body: The well-diving event was cancelled after the first competitor demonstrated, conclusively, that the well is deep. He has been declared winner in absentia and is expected to resurface at some point. Bucket service resumes after the ceremony.

sports.head: GOBLINS LOSE A FRIENDLY NOBODY BOOKED
sports.body: A visiting goblin squad arrived for what they described as a siege and found themselves in a fixture against the drawbridge. Final score Drawbridge 11, Goblins 0. Goblin management have lodged a complaint written mostly in screaming.

sports.head: PUMP-STACK ENDURANCE: STILL GOING
sports.body: Entrants in the pump-stack endurance trial have been operating the screw pump for three months. Organisers have lost track of who is competing and who was simply assigned the job. Either way, the reservoir is lovely and nobody is allowed to leave.

sports.head: ELVES OFFER 'TREE-HUGGING' AS SPORT
sports.body: A visiting elven delegation proposed tree-hugging as a new league event. The sports committee laughed for eleven minutes, then felled the tree to build the scoreboard. The elves left early, citing irreconcilable differences about lumber.

sports.head: CAT-WRANGLING CUP DECIDED BY CATS
sports.body: With {cats} cats now in residence, the cat-wrangling cup has become a numbers game the dwarves are losing. Final tally: dwarves 2 cats wrangled, cats 31 dwarves adopted. Next year's event will be held, as always, wherever the cats decide.

sports.head: DOGS DOMINATE HAULING HEAT
sports.body: The {dogs} fortress dogs won the hauling heat by default after refusing to haul anything, which judges admitted was a cleaner performance than most dwarves managed. Each dog was awarded a bone, which they then hauled. Sort of.

sports.head: MOST VALUABLE PLAYER NAMED
sports.body: {citizen} has been named Most Valuable Player for the season, chiefly for showing up. Teammates praised a consistent work ethic and an ability to sleep on any surface, including the pitch. The trophy has been engraved and promptly used as a mug.

sports.head: STRIKE-THE-EARTH SPRINT RESULT
sports.body: The opening sprint to dig the first staircase was won with a pick in record time, then disqualified when the runner struck an aquifer and finished the race swimming. Officials ruled it 'technically a different sport' and awarded half marks.

sports.head: INFANT JOINS MILITIA BY ACCIDENT
sports.body: A militia sparring session gained an unexpected member when a mother reported for duty with her baby in hand. The infant blocked two strikes and was named rookie of the month. Doctors say both are fine; the dummy is not.

sports.head: WRESTLING RULEBOOK AMENDED AGAIN
sports.body: The danger-room wrestling rulebook now forbids biting, gouging, and pinching an opponent's beard into a knot. It continues to permit throwing an opponent into a pond, provided it is a nice pond. The amendment passed 7-3 with one abstention from the pond.

sports.head: CARAVAN GUARDS PLAY EXHIBITION MATCH
sports.body: Guards from the latest caravan played an exhibition match against the fortress reserves at the trade depot. Score: Reserves 2, Guards 2, Wagon 1. Several goods were lost to enthusiastic tackling and are now classed as souvenirs.

sports.head: MIGRANT TRIALS UNCOVER NEW TALENT
sports.body: Open trials for the new migrants unearthed a remarkable cheese maker, two competent fishers and a dwarf who can lift a barrel with his beard. Coaches are unsure which sport this qualifies for but have signed him anyway.

sports.head: MAGMA HOPSCOTCH BANNED PERMANENTLY
sports.body: The fortress council has permanently banned magma hopscotch after a season with zero completed games. The hopscotch grid has been converted into a smelter. Officials note that, in a sense, everyone who played is still contributing.

sports.head: NAPPING LEAGUE ENDS IN DEADLOCK
sports.body: The competitive napping final went into a fourth day before referees woke up and realised they had been competing too. The match was declared a draw and everyone agreed to have another go after a short rest.

sports.head: HAULING RELAY REMATCH CALLED OFF
sports.body: The relay rematch was called off when all eight runners were reassigned mid-race to carry {stone} to a distant stockpile. Fans described the result as 'just a normal Tuesday'. The stone was delivered in good order. The race was not.

sports.head: NOBLE MANDATES NEW OFFSIDE RULE
sports.body: A noble has mandated that no player may stand within ten urists of the ball unless it is made of gold. As no ball is made of gold, the season has been played entirely from the stands. Attendance figures are excellent.

sports.head: FORGOTTEN BEAST STORMS THE PITCH
sports.body: Play was suspended after a forgotten beast wandered onto the field, ate the referee's whistle, and sneezed something unpleasant on the goalposts. The beast was later shown a red card, which it also ate. Match abandoned at Fortress 1, Beast 1.

sports.head: SPRINTERS IN FULL ARMOR: A MISTAKE
sports.body: The new full-plate sprint was won in just under a season. Competitors rattled audibly the entire distance, prompting complaints from the library. Next year organisers plan to allow helmets only, or possibly just a firm hat.

sports.head: BARD HIRED AS MATCH COMMENTATOR
sports.body: The tavern's resident bard has been hired to commentate league matches. Fans report that his description of a goalless draw ran to forty verses and included a lament for the ball. He is being paid in dwarven wine and is not complaining.

sports.head: MATCH FORFEITED: TOO MANY CATS ON PITCH
sports.body: Saturday's fixture was forfeited when the pitch became 70 percent cat. Groundskeepers attempted to clear the field and were adopted. The visiting side asked whether the cats count as fans or players. Nobody has an answer.

sports.head: KOBOLDS WIN TROPHY BY STEALING IT
sports.body: A kobold thief entered the trophy room and left with the season's championship cup, making kobolds the first side to win a title without playing a game. League officials say the result will stand because chasing them seemed like a lot of effort.

sports.head: WINTER GAMES MOVED INDOORS, OBVIOUSLY
sports.body: The winter games have been moved underground after the outdoor events produced eleven frozen competitors and one very confused yak. Organisers admit they should have checked whether dwarves like the sky. They do not, and in winter the sky does not like them either.

sports.head: SPRING SEASON OPENS WITH A THUD
sports.body: The spring season opened with the traditional ceremonial dropping of a log down the central shaft. It landed, as ever, on the ceremonial planner. The crowd cheered, the planner waved weakly, and the league is officially under way.

sports.head: SUMMER MUDBALL GETS OUT OF HAND
sports.body: Summer's mudball tournament ended when the mud reached the dining hall and was mistaken for a meal. Several spectators reported it as 'fine, but under-seasoned'. The tournament will resume once the cook stops serving the pitch.

sports.head: AUTUMN LEAF-CATCHING DECLARED UNSAFE
sports.body: The autumn leaf-catching contest was declared unsafe after three competitors went outside, looked up, and fainted at the sight of the open sky. The surviving entrant caught one leaf and is being treated for nerves.

sports.head: NEW CAPTAIN TAKES THE ARMBAND
sports.body: Following a promotion, {promoted} has been named captain and has already introduced a strict new training regime of sitting, eating and nodding thoughtfully. Squad morale has never been higher. Squad fitness has never been lower.

sports.head: BREWERS CREDIT BARRELS FOR WIN STREAK
sports.body: The Brewers extended their win streak to nine, a run their captain credits to the fortress's {drinks} drinks in stock. 'We play better when we can't see straight,' he said, before walking confidently into a wall.

sports.head: SEASON IN DOUBT AS BARRELS RUN DRY
sports.body: With drink stocks dangerously low, the league has suspended all fixtures until further notice. Several players report being too sober to tell which end of the pitch is theirs. Brewers are working double shifts and refusing to referee.

sports.head: TRAINING DUMMY ANNOUNCES RETIREMENT
sports.body: After four seasons and roughly twelve thousand blows, the fortress's longest-serving training dummy has announced its retirement. It says it will spend its time 'standing very still somewhere quiet'. A testimonial match is planned, which it will also lose.

obits.text: {deadname} has {cause}. A devoted {prof}, they once owned forty socks and could name every one. Mourners are invited to bring a single clean sock to the memorial. Odd ones especially welcome.

The fortress mourns {deadname}, a {prof} who ate a plump helmet every day and described each one as 'the best yet'. They {cause} doing what they loved, or near enough. A small mushroom has been planted in their honour.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. Famed for an excellent overarm throw during tantrums, they leave behind one dented door and many fond memories of ducking. The dining hall will hold a moment of silence and absolutely no mugs.

Farewell to {deadname}, who spent many happy hours admiring a particularly fine wall. A thoughtful {prof}, they {cause} quietly. The wall, which was engraved with a picture of a wall, has been dedicated to them.

{deadname}, beloved {prof} and owner of eleven cats, has {cause}. The cats have been distributed among friends, who did not volunteer. The cats, for their part, seem to have already moved on, which is how cats grieve.

We say goodbye to {deadname}, a {prof} who once hauled a single pebble across the entire fortress with total dedication. They have {cause}. The pebble has been placed on their slab, finally in the right stockpile.

{deadname} has {cause}. A proud {prof} with a beard that could be seen from two rooms away, they are survived by a comb, a mirror, and a great many admirers. The beard was, we are assured, magnificent to the end.

The tavern is quieter without {deadname}, a {prof} and part-time wine critic who rated every barrel 'acceptable, more please'. They {cause} surrounded by friends. A toast will be drunk in their honour, then several more.

{deadname}, a {prof}, has {cause}. They spent a lifetime in a dignified feud with the carp of the lower river and never once won. The carp have declined to comment but were seen looking somewhat smug.

Rest well, {deadname}. A cautious {prof} who never once looked at the sky and said it was 'too much ceiling missing', they {cause} well below ground, exactly as they would have wanted. A roof has been added to their memorial.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. A fixture of the meeting hall, they could talk for hours about the weather without ever having seen it. Their usual chair will remain empty, though the cats have already claimed it.

The fortress bids farewell to {deadname}, a {prof} who has {cause}. Friends ask that a slab be engraved promptly, as they always hated waiting and we would prefer they did not come back to complain about it.

{deadname} has {cause}. A meticulous {prof}, they once spent a full season organising the bin of left boots. Their own coffin is labelled, alphabetised and colour-coded, exactly as specified in a letter found in their pocket.

We remember {deadname}, a {prof} so gentle they apologised to boulders before mining them. They have {cause}. The miners have agreed to say sorry to one rock each this week in their honour. Most rocks appear to accept.

{deadname}, {prof} and enthusiastic dancer, has {cause}. Their signature move, the Stumbling Urist, was performed nightly whether music was playing or not. The tavern floor still bears the scuff marks. They will not be polished out.

The overseer's office regrets to report that {deadname}, a {prof}, has {cause}. They were punctual, polite, and once filled in a form correctly on the first try, a feat not since repeated. Their paperwork is complete. We miss them.

Farewell to {deadname}, who told the same story about a giant cave spider at every meal for six years. A dear {prof}, they have {cause}. The spider has grown three sizes in the retelling. It will continue to grow.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. They baked a biscuit so hard it was used as a doorstop for two seasons and later as a training shield. It sits proudly beside their slab. Nobody is allowed to eat it, as nobody could.
{fort} has lost one of its own. {deadname}, a {prof}, has {cause}. They once called {fort} 'the second-best hole in the world', which from a dwarf is high praise. The best hole remains unidentified.

The library mourns {deadname}, a {prof} who borrowed one book and kept it for nine years. They {cause} with the book close at hand. It has been returned with no late fee, because the librarian is sentimental.

{deadname} has {cause}. A kind {prof}, they named every dog in the fortress, often the same name twice. The dogs will be looked after. Several have been seen sitting by the door, which dogs do anyway, but still.

We bid farewell to {deadname}, a {prof} who heckled every goblin siege from the battlements with remarkable vocabulary. They have {cause}. The goblins, we hear, were quietly relieved. The rest of us will miss the shouting.

{deadname}, the fortress's most loyal visitor to the well, has {cause}. A thoughtful {prof}, they drew water every morning and spoke to the bucket like an old friend. The bucket appears to be taking it hard.

This {season}, we say goodbye to {deadname}, a {prof} who loved the season for reasons nobody could explain. They have {cause}. Their friends will mark the date each year with a small, confused celebration.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. Their one strange mood produced a slightly lopsided bracelet they insisted was 'about feelings'. It is now displayed in the meeting hall, where it is still slightly lopsided and still about feelings.

The tavern falls quiet for {deadname}, a {prof} who sang loudly, frequently and in no recognisable key. They have {cause}. The bard has written a tribute song and, out of respect, will perform it badly.

{deadname} has {cause}. A fastidious {prof}, they filed twenty-two complaints about miasma, all of them correct. In their honour, someone has finally cleaned the refuse pile. They would be pleased, and also say it took long enough.

Farewell to {deadname}, a {prof} who believed elves were 'just very tall rumours'. They have {cause}. A tree was nearly planted in their honour, until friends remembered how they felt about trees. A nice rock was chosen instead.

{deadname}, {prof}, has {cause}. A well-known face at the hospital, they had been splinted, sutured and bandaged so often that the doctor kept a bed reserved. The bed will stay made up a while longer, out of habit.

{citizen} delivered a moving eulogy for {deadname}, a {prof} who has {cause}. The speech was brief, heartfelt and only interrupted twice by a cat. Everyone agreed it was exactly what {deadname} would have wanted, cat included.
We remember {deadname}, a {prof} and early champion of minecart travel who always said brakes were 'for the timid'. They have {cause}. The track has been renamed in their honour and now has a brake.

{deadname}, a quiet {prof}, has {cause}. They made the fortress's finest cheese and never once told anyone the recipe. A search of their quarters found only a note reading 'more cheese'. We believe that was the recipe.

gossip.text: Overheard in the Meeting Hall: {citizen} and {citizen2} were seen sharing a table at dinner, then a bench, then a single plump helmet. Tongues are wagging. Beards are being groomed. A wedding betting pool has opened.
{citizen} turned heads this week in a bold new hat of unclear origin. Fashion insiders say it is either very daring or a bucket. {citizen} declined to comment and walked into a doorframe.
A feud has erupted between two cat owners over who owns the orange cat. The cat has not commented, as it is currently living with a third party who did not ask for it.

Society watchers note that the baron skipped the latest banquet, citing 'insufficient gold in the furniture'. Guests said the food was lovely and, without the baron, nobody was mandated to make anything out of bronze.

Overheard at the tavern: {citizen} read a love poem aloud to {citizen2}, who listened politely before pointing out it rhymed 'granite' with 'granite'. The poem has been submitted to the library anyway.
The latest craze sweeping the fortress is the triple beard braid. Early adopters report that it looks wonderful but takes an entire morning and cannot be undone without professional help or a pick.
A quiet war rages over the best seat in the dining hall, the one nearest the barrels. Sources say it has changed hands eleven times this month, usually during someone's nap.

Someone left a finely cut gem on {citizen}'s bed with a note reading 'from an admirer'. The jeweller insists it was not him. The bookkeeper insists it was not from the stockpile. Nobody believes either.
Rumour has it a dwarf was seen being polite to an elven trader. Friends insist it was a misunderstanding caused by bad lighting. The dwarf has gone into hiding behind a large barrel.

The fortress's exclusive wine-tasting society has admitted its first new member in years. Initiation reportedly involves drinking an entire barrel and then pretending you could taste the 'notes of cave moss'.
Tension between two master masons reached boiling point when one engraved the other's portrait onto a latrine wall. The subject of the portrait called it 'unflattering but technically superb'.

Overheard in the nursery: a new parent is considering naming the baby after the fortress's favourite boulder. Grandparents are lobbying for something more traditional, such as Urist, which is also what the boulder is called.
{citizen} has accused {citizen2} of taking a single sock from the clothing bin. {citizen2} counters that socks cannot be stolen, only 'reassigned'. The sock remains at large.
Hospital staff report that one patient has broken the same toe three times this season, each time requesting the same doctor. The doctor has started to suspect it is not about the toe.

The meeting hall hosted an impromptu dance this week after a bard played something nearly cheerful. Witnesses describe the dancing as 'loud', 'heavy' and 'mostly stomping'. Two cats were briefly involved.
The bookkeeper is said to be smitten with someone, judging by a sudden habit of counting every item twice when they walk past. The stock records have never been more accurate, or more wrong.
Insiders reveal the overseer has given up dwarven wine for a whole week. Staff report productivity is up, laughter is down, and three chairs have been thrown so far, not all by the overseer.

A dwarf has apparently been writing letters to a goblin captured last siege. The letters are mostly about cooking. The goblin's replies are mostly about escaping, but they are getting longer and friendlier.
Wedding bells may soon ring for {citizen} and {citizen2}, who were seen choosing a coffin together, a deeply romantic gesture in dwarven culture. Guests are advised to bring their own mugs.
Overheard outside the craftsdwarf's workshop: a muttered list of 'shells, bones, something red, more red'. Friends are keeping a respectful distance and quietly hiding anything red.
A garden party was attempted on the surface this week. Guests lasted six minutes before a cloud moved, at which point everyone fled indoors. The cake is still up there, being admired by birds.

A newly made masterwork chair has caused a stir. Several dwarves have asked to sit in it. Its maker has refused all requests, explaining that the chair is 'not for sitting, it is for feeling things about'.
{citizen} has been humming the same tune in the corridors for a fortnight. Neighbours describe it as catchy at first, then haunting, and now possibly a form of siege warfare.
The trade depot was busier than usual this season, mostly because a handsome caravan guard was leaning on a wagon. Sales of beads went up four hundred percent. The guard bought nothing.
The new arrivals are causing a stir in the meeting hall. One of them has already claimed the good bedroom, the good chair, and, according to {citizen}, the good gossip spot. Tensions are rising.
Since the promotion, {promoted} has been spotted walking in a more important way. Friends say the strut is new, the frown is new, and the demand for a bigger mug is very new.
A rumour that someone has dyed their beard with plump helmet juice was confirmed this week when a dwarf with a purple beard walked through the dining hall to stunned silence and one slow clap.
Overheard at the kennels: the dogs are said to be organising against the cats. Sources say the plan involves barking, then more barking, and then lying down because it is warm by the fire.
A fisher claims to have seen a carp wink at him. Fellow fishers dismiss the story, though several have stopped fishing alone, and one has started wearing a helmet near water.

{citizen} gave {citizen2} a carved stone mug as a gift. {citizen2} gave {citizen} the exact same mug back the following week, insisting it was a coincidence. Friends are calling it 'the mug situation'.
The library has a new rule: no talking, no shouting, and absolutely no reading aloud of tavern menus. The rule was adopted after an incident involving a dramatic recital of the drinks list.
Two cheese makers are no longer speaking after a disagreement about whether cheese should be 'firm' or 'very firm'. Both have been seen sulking in their workshops. The cheese is unaffected.
A dwarf who threw a mug at the meeting hall statue last month has formally apologised to it. The statue accepted, according to the dwarf, who says it 'gave a very forgiving look'.
Overheard in the craftsdwarf's corridor: {masterwright} has mentioned their recent masterpiece to every passer-by, three cats and one confused goat. The goat was reportedly impressed.
Social circles are buzzing over who has been sleeping on the dining hall floor instead of in their bedroom. Insiders say it is 'about being near the food' and 'nothing personal against beds'.
Capes are back in fashion this season, according to several dwarves who have tripped over theirs on the stairs. The hospital reports a capes-related spike in sprained ankles and wounded pride.
Overheard near the tombs: someone claims to have heard a ghost complaining about the draught. Friends say this is either a genuine haunting or the miner who sleeps in the crypt to save walking.

weather_jokes.text: Rain expected on the surface. Fortunately, the surface is where dwarves keep the elves and the things they do not care about.
Light rain today. Dwarves who forgot to bathe last year are encouraged to step outside briefly. Very briefly.
Showers expected, which the refuse pile will treat as a spa day. Expect a stronger aroma near the depot by evening.
Heavy rain means the river rises and so does the carp's confidence. Fishers are advised to keep a sturdy stick nearby.
Wet weather on the surface. Woodcutters will be damp, grumpy and still cutting trees. The elves will be damp and still upset about it.
Snow on the surface. Beards left outside may freeze into interesting shapes. Hairdressers will be on standby at the main entrance.
Snow is falling out of the sky, which dwarves already distrusted for having nothing holding it up. This confirms everything.
Heavy snow today. Haulers carrying logs from the surface will return as small, angry snowdrifts. Please do not stockpile them.
Cold snap expected. The well may freeze, so drink your water early. Or skip it entirely and drink wine, as tradition intended.
Snow and bitter winds forecast. Wear your socks. Both of them. If you only have one sock, wear it with confidence.
Clear skies forecast, meaning a lot of sky with nothing in it. Dwarves of a nervous disposition should remain indoors and look at a nice ceiling.
Sunny today. The big yellow light will be out again. Nobody knows what it wants. Do not make eye contact.
Fine weather on the surface, perfect for elves to stand around being pleased with trees. Dwarves are advised to stay below and be pleased with rocks.
Clear skies and dry roads mean a caravan could arrive any day. Hide the good mugs and polish the mediocre ones.
Pleasant weather forecast, which goblins also enjoy. Expect excellent visibility for any siege that happens to wander by.
Underground forecast: dark, still and pleasantly rocky, as always. Chance of cave-in: low. Chance of a cat underfoot: certain.
Lower levels remain warm thanks to the magma. Dwarves are reminded that warm is good and molten is too much.
Humid conditions in the caverns with scattered fungus. Visibility poor, forgotten beasts possible. A normal day.
A miasma front is moving in from the butcher's shop. Expect queasy feelings in the dining hall by lunch.
Tavern forecast: heavy drinking expected after dark, with a high chance of singing and scattered mugs by midnight.
Today's weather on the surface: {weather}. Below ground: rock, mostly. We recommend the rock.
It is {season} in {fort}. On the surface this means something. Down here it means the same as every other season: digging.
A low-pressure tantrum system is building near the noble quarters. Mugs may fall in scattered bursts. Helmets advised.
Damp conditions continue near the aquifer, as they have since the miner said 'just one more tile'. Bring a bucket.
Winter has arrived. Dwarves are advised to stay warm, stay underground, and stay near the still.
Summer heat on the surface. The farmers report the crops are growing, the farmers are sweating, and the sky remains suspicious.
Autumn: leaves falling from trees. Woodcutters say this is the trees giving up early. Elves call it beautiful. Both are tiresome.
Spring thaw underway. Rivers rising, ice melting, and the carp are back and in a mood. Mind your ankles.

corrections.text: In our last issue we reported that a carp had been elected mayor. The carp was in fact only nominated. We regret the error, and so, we hear, does the carp.
A previous article stated the tavern serves water. It does not. It has never served water. We apologise to the tavern for any damage to its reputation.
Last week we described a visiting elf as 'taller than a door'. He was taller than a short door. We stand by the general tone of the remark.
We previously reported that the fortress had 112 socks. The correct figure is 112 single socks and zero pairs. The Herald regrets any false hope this may have caused.
A caption last issue identified a statue as the baron. It was a boulder. The baron has asked us to clarify that he is 'considerably more impressive than a boulder'.
Our previous issue described the sky as 'mostly harmless'. Following a large number of complaints, we now acknowledge the sky is unsettling and we regret making light of it.
An article claimed the fortress's oldest cheese was three years old. It is seven. It is also, according to the cook, 'gaining opinions'. We apologise to the cheese.
We incorrectly described last month's siege as 'a friendly visit'. The goblins were not friendly. We apologise to readers and to the drawbridge, which did all the work.
Last issue's recipe for 'Roasted Plump Helmet' accidentally listed 'one granite boulder' as an ingredient. Please do not add the boulder. The two readers who did are recovering.
We misspelled Urist as 'Urist' in last week's issue. We meant to write Urist. We apologise to Urist, Urist, and the other Urist.
Our census reported a cat population of four. This was an estimate made in a single room. The true figure is unknown and growing even as we print this correction.
An events listing advertised a 'relaxing dip in the magma pool'. This was a printing error. There is no relaxing dip. Please stay away from the magma pool.
A previous article described a legendary artifact as 'a nice hat'. It is a legendary artifact. Its maker would like it known that it is also, in fairness, quite a nice hat.
Last week's forecast predicted 'rain of rocks'. This was a misreading of our cave-in report. We apologise, and also, please check the ceiling in the east corridor.
We reported that two dwarves had purchased a coffin together as a romantic gesture. They had in fact bought it as a table. Congratulations on the table.
Our profile of a craftsdwarf said they were 'in a strange mood'. We meant the fey kind, not the grumpy kind. They are now in the grumpy kind, about the article.
The scoreline Militia 3, Training Dummy 0 was misprinted. The dummy did not score; it simply fell over onto the captain. The result stands, as does the dummy.
We described the overseer as 'napping on the job'. The overseer has clarified that he was 'resting his eyes strategically'. We apologise for any implication of napping.
Our previous issue gave the fortress population as one hundred. The correct figure is {pop}. We counted the cats and one particularly sociable goat by mistake.
We dated last week's issue in the wrong year. It is year {year}. Several readers who believed they had time-travelled are asked to calm down and return to work.
Last issue's opinion piece suggested that trees have feelings. This view was submitted by an elf posing as a dwarf in a fake beard. The beard has been confiscated.
Our health column advised drinking 'at least one cup of water daily'. This was a typo for 'wine'. The hospital wishes to say it disagrees with both us and itself.
Last week's business report was written by a kobold who had stolen our office's quill. The stated market price of copper, 'shiny, very shiny', was inaccurate.
We wrongly named last season's forgotten beast as 'Gerald'. The beast's actual name is far longer and mostly vowels. Gerald, a local miner, would like his name back.
We reported that the dining hall had moved. The dining hall has not moved. A sleepy dwarf merely walked into the wrong room and ate a stockpile of turnips.
Our review called the bard's latest song 'mercifully short'. This was an error. It was not short. We regret the word 'short'. We stand by 'mercifully'.
Our headline 'STRIKE THE EARTH!' was misread by several miners as an instruction. The earth is fine. The miners have been asked to put down their picks and breathe.
